story_beats.title: BONKULA DIBBA · THE ACCOUNT BOOK
story_beats.line: At Bonkula Dibba, Gireesam admits that the twenty rupees he took from Pootakullamma for provisions went on dancing girls. Their argument has made staying unsafe; he plans to leave by way of his pupil, Venkatesam.
choices: Read the debt as a plain entry
Recast the account as a grand theory
story_beats.response: The ledger stays stubbornly ordinary. Gireesam's explanation does not repay it.

story_beats.title: THE TUTOR'S AUDIENCE
story_beats.line: Gireesam puts on mock scholarship, switching into grand English-backed claims to keep Venkatesam listening. The boy answers with the practical truth: his tutor has scarcely taught him a lesson.
story_beats.response: The speech grows; the syllabus does not. The joke is Gireesam's pretension, not the boy's poor result.

story_beats.title: EVERYTHING IS A TEACHING AID
story_beats.line: Under the tutor story, Gireesam solicits books, cash, sweets, cigars, and transport. He dresses each want as educational necessity while preparing to leave town with Venkatesam.
choices: Arrange the requests as a lesson plan
Count each request without the lecture
story_beats.response: The list is clear; the scholarship remains a performance. Nothing here earns a reward for the deception.

story_beats.title: A ROUTE, NOT A VICTORY
story_beats.line: The route turns from Bonkula Dibba toward Madhuravani's room. Gireesam has an exit plan, not a moral triumph; the next scene changes focus to Madhuravani.
choices: Give the road one last grand title
story_beats.response: The departure leads into another person's story.
